_meta.note: Add an honest security note for the MCP server and link it from the related how-tos. The note is a mechanism how-to backed by the EXISTING proof docs/howto/gate-examples/mcp-http.sh (MCP-HTTP-SECURE-OK already asserts Origin-403 + --allow-remote refusal + the exact-loopback allowlist), so every security CLAIM it makes is gate-verified — no new proof, and no overclaim beyond what the code proves. Accurate posture: stdio has no network surface (preferred); the HTTP transport is unauthenticated by design → loopback-only default, refuses non-loopback bind without --allow-remote, validates Origin (DNS-rebinding). Trust model: a caller cannot fabricate a gate pass (behavioral gate + distinct-actor review artifact), but CAN mutate state and, via the `gate` tool, trigger execution of the DAG's gate shell-commands — so the server is as trusted as whoever can reach it, and dag.json is trusted input. Also refresh the related MCP how-tos (drive-heartbeat-over-mcp.md, install-the-heartbeat-plugin.md, keep-stage-b-untrusted.md) to link the note and fix a stale suite-ref in howto-list. Docs-only; suites stay green; prose-integrity enforced.

tasks.title: Author secure-the-mcp-server.md
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/secure-the-mcp-server.md. Cover, accurately to the code: (1) what a caller CAN'T do — fabricate a gate pass (behavioral gate + distinct-actor review artifact; link keep-stage-b-untrusted.md); (2) what a caller CAN do — mutate state and, via the `gate` tool, trigger the DAG's gate shell-commands, so the server is as trusted as whoever can reach it and dag.json is trusted input; (3) transports — stdio (default, no network surface, preferred) vs HTTP (--http, unauthenticated by design); (4) built-in HTTP hardening — loopback-only default, refuses non-loopback --host without --allow-remote, validates Origin (exact-loopback match, DNS-rebinding defense), citing the proof gate-examples/mcp-http.sh; (5) if you must expose it — put it behind a reverse proxy that authenticates + terminates TLS (the server has no auth of its own), keep dag.json trusted, prefer stdio. Only real commands; every security claim must be one the proof already verifies (no overclaim).
